title: Admin Toolkit: Runbook-as-Task Orchestrator for Escalation Playbooks
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a lightweight orchestrator that treats runbooks as first-class tasks, enabling safe, auditable escalation playbooks that can be executed, paused, and remediated with built-in observability and deterministic retries. This ticket covers the runtime shim, task schema, telemetry hooks, and a canary simulation environment for validation.
background: On-call engineers frequently run multi-step escalation procedures that mix API calls, infra checks, and human approvals. Current runbook docs live in Confluence and are executed ad-hoc; we lack a taskable runtime with strong observability and safety gates. This increases mean-time-to-resolution and makes post-incident analysis manual and error-prone.
goals: 1) Define a compact task schema for runbook steps (idempotency token, inputs, safe-mode flag). 2) Build an orchestrator service that executes steps as discrete tasks with pause/resume, explicit audit events, and credential blinding for secrets. 3) Add telemetry: per-step latency, success/failure reason, token-level cost estimate. 4) Provide a canary simulator (synthetic incidents) so teams can validate runbooks without hitting prod infra.
non_goals: Not building an LLM-based autopilot in this task. Not replacing the existing incident management system; this integrates with PagerDuty only for trigger hooks.
success_criteria: Ship task schema v1 and document in Console docs
Orchestrator runs can execute a 5-step escalation playbook in <120s total wall time (non-blocking steps allowed)
Every executed step emits audit events to our logging pipeline and appears on Console trace view
Canary simulator can run 20 synthetic playbooks/day without requiring infra changes
Postmortem templates auto-populate with executed step logs for at least two pilot teams
technical_approach:
- Task Schema: JSON-LD-ish flat schema with required fields (step_id, action, idempotency_key, timeout_ms, retry_policy, safe_mode boolean).
- Orchestrator: stateless web service + durable step queue (use existing task-queue infra). Step executor implements guarded adapters for common actions (k8s rollout, infra queries, escalation-API, shell command via sandbox).
- Safety: secret references resolved from EphemeralKV; any action requiring elevated permissions must pass an approval token.
- Telemetry: emit structured events (step.start, step.end, step.error) to telemetry-ingest with ctx fields (runbook_id, exec_id, step_index). Include token-metering estimate stubs for cost modelling.
- Simulation: a local sandbox harness that replays steps against mocked adapters and validates side effects, with fail-fast validation for known anti-patterns (non-idempotent shell calls, long sleeps).
user_flow: Engineer selects saved runbook in Console and clicks 'Execute as Task'
Orchestrator creates an exec_id, enqueues steps and returns a modal with live step logs
If a step requires approval, the UI shows an approval card and pauses until approver accepts
Upon completion, the modal links to a scoped audit view and pre-filled postmortem draft
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal SRE team only, feature-flagged; runbooks are read-only conversions of Confluence docs
Beta: two pilot product teams (Search + DevTools) with optional canary simulation runs
GA: enable for all teams after 4 weeks of telemetry and two retrospective cycles
open_questions: What is the minimal approval UX that satisfies legal/regulatory teams for Private deployments?
Should the orchestrator persist step outputs or only return ephemeral logs to reduce sensitive data surface?
Do we need RBAC bindings per-runbook or reuse existing RBAC in Console?
decisions: Use existing task-queue infra (TaskQ) rather than introducing a new orchestrator store
Persist only metadata and audit pointers to logs; avoid writing raw secrets to the runbook execution records
Simulations run against mocked adapters and will not call external systems by default (opt-in for advanced testing)
